items.note: The page assembles the whole step: digits in base 2^b, the degree chain 2q-2<2n/b<=T/2<S, and the coefficient bound. It also spells out why cyclic and ordinary convolution agree, as the assignment asked: "If every i+k that occurs is below S, the congruence forces i+k=j".
It gives b=ceil(log_2 n), q=ceil(n/b) blocks with 0<=u_i<2^b, U=u(2^b), and shows UV=c(2^b) with c_j=sum_{i+k=j}u_i v_k, which matches the paper's radix-digit polynomials.

Each link of the chain is justified: "q<n/b+1 gives 2q-2<2n/b", T>=4n/b gives 2n/b<=T/2, and T/2<S comes from the parameter choice. Reduction modulo x^S-1 is explained as collecting the terms with i+k congruent to j mod S, so there is no wraparound. This matches the paper.

It says each c_j is a sum of at most q digit products, each in [0,(2^b-1)^2]. It justifies q<=n<=2^b "because b>=1 and b>=log_2 n" and concludes q(2^b-1)^2<2^b*2^{2b}=2^{3b}, which matches the paper's (eq:capacity).
